units.source_excerpt: Three very natural questions arise regarding this data
units.function: open by numbering the questions the data raises
units.reusable_pattern: List the questions as (1), (2), (3) before any model.
information_order: three very natural questions arise
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open the summary with the method.

units.source_excerpt: we develop a comprehensive Bayesian model consisting of three submodels
units.function: name the model by how many parts it has
units.reusable_pattern: Say consisting of three submodels, then name what each predicts.
information_order: consisting of three submodels which predict
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the three predictions into one claim.

units.source_excerpt: Most notably, we formulate a novel Wordle-specific entropy measure we call Subset Entropy
units.function: name a new quantity and say what it quantifies
units.reusable_pattern: Use most notably, we formulate, we call.
information_order: most notably we formulate we call
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the measure standard.

units.source_excerpt: We use a preliminary Lasso regression to isolate the most relevant predictors, which we then use
units.function: mark one method as preliminary to the next
units.reusable_pattern: Call the selector preliminary, then say which we then use.
information_order: preliminary, which we then use
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the lasso as the final model.

units.source_excerpt: they are conditionally independent given the data, making it efficient to sample
units.function: give the structural fact that makes the sampler cheap
units.reusable_pattern: State the independence, then making it efficient.
information_order: conditionally independent given the data, making it efficient
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the submodels are independent of the data.

units.source_excerpt: Under the assumption that the Times choose words randomly, this can be interpreted as a causal effect
units.function: turn a correlation into a cause only under a named assumption
units.reusable_pattern: Name the assumption, then this can be interpreted as.
information_order: under the assumption, this can be interpreted as a causal effect
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the assumption.

units.source_excerpt: Our model is able to predict outcomes for new data and retrodict for old data
units.function: pair prediction with a check on the past
units.reusable_pattern: Use predict for new data and retrodict for old data.
information_order: predict for new, retrodict for old
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report only the future interval.

units.source_excerpt: Our model gives gives a 95% prediction interval
units.function: report an interval and keep the doubled verb
units.reusable_pattern: Keep gives gives. Give the interval, the word, and the date together.
information_order: gives gives a 95% prediction interval
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repair the doubled verb.

units.source_excerpt: our model does not just provide such simple point estimates and prediction intervals, but full posterior distributions
units.function: refuse the point estimate in favor of the whole distribution
units.reusable_pattern: Use not just, but.
information_order: not just, but full posterior distributions
prohibited_generalizations: Do not stop at the interval.

units.source_excerpt: The goal of the game is simple to understand
units.function: call the rules simple before stating them
units.reusable_pattern: Say simple to understand, then state the rule.
information_order: simple to understand, then the rule
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open with the data set.

units.source_excerpt: At the the start of each day there is a 5-letter target word
units.function: state the daily object and keep the doubled article
units.reusable_pattern: Keep at the the start.
information_order: at the the start of each day
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repair the doubled article.

units.source_excerpt: For a person to randomly guess a target word in six tries would statistically be almost impossible
units.function: dismiss random guessing so the feedback has a job
units.reusable_pattern: Call the unaided task almost impossible, then name what changes it.
information_order: would statistically be almost impossible
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the game is hard without the contrast.

units.source_excerpt: This, however, is where tile color feedback comes into play
units.function: pivot from impossibility to the information the game returns
units.reusable_pattern: Use this, however, is where.
information_order: this however is where comes into play
prohibited_generalizations: Do not explain the tiles before the pivot.

units.source_excerpt: With this information, most players are able to guess the word from thousands of possibilities within six tries
units.function: credit the feedback, not the player
units.reusable_pattern: Start with with this information.
information_order: with this information, most players are able
prohibited_generalizations: Do not credit skill alone.

units.source_excerpt: One Twitter account that has popped up as a result of this trend is @WordleStats
units.function: name the data source as a consequence of the trend
units.reusable_pattern: Say has popped up as a result, then name the account.
information_order: has popped up as a result of this trend
reusable_elements: has popped up as a result
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the bot as an official source.

units.source_excerpt: the resulting inferred difficulty of target words gleamed from this data
units.function: say the difficulty is inferred, and keep the verb
units.reusable_pattern: Keep gleamed. Call the difficulty inferred.
information_order: inferred difficulty gleamed from this data
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repair gleamed, and do not call the difficulty observed directly.

units.source_excerpt: We fixed several errors that appear in the provided data. These are logged below for full transparency
units.function: announce a repair list and the reason for printing it
units.reusable_pattern: Say we fixed, then logged below for full transparency.
information_order: logged below for full transparency
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide a changed cell.

units.source_excerpt: we divided the percentages in each row by their sum to obtain proportions
units.function: repair rounded percentages before turning them into counts
units.reusable_pattern: Divide by the row sum first, because the printed percentages need not sum to 100.
information_order: divided by their sum to obtain proportions
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat rounded percentages as proportions.

units.source_excerpt: Add 1 back to the counts, in order from the count which was rounded down most
units.function: give the rounding rule that restores the daily total
units.reusable_pattern: State the order: most remainder first, until the total matches.
information_order: in order from the count which was rounded down most
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round independently and ignore the daily total.

units.source_excerpt: This method gives counts which correspond to the given percentages, are integers, and whose sum is the number of reports
units.function: list the three properties the repair must keep
units.reusable_pattern: Close the method with which correspond, are, and whose.
information_order: which correspond, are integers, and whose sum
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the counts are the true unrounded counts.

units.source_excerpt: which provides a good approximation of the set of words that a player could guess
units.function: justify an external word list as an approximation
units.reusable_pattern: Call the list a good approximation, not the true set.
information_order: provides a good approximation of the set
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the wordbank as exhaustive.

units.source_excerpt: which we take to be a set of common guess words
units.function: turn a ranking into a working set, and say so
units.reusable_pattern: Use which we take to be.
information_order: which we take to be
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the thirty words are what players actually guess.

units.source_excerpt: which gives a somewhat naive but reasonable metric to evaluate guess words
units.function: admit a metric is naive and keep it anyway
units.reusable_pattern: Say somewhat naive but reasonable.
information_order: somewhat naive but reasonable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not defend the metric as optimal.

units.source_excerpt: intuitively seems to be difficult for a variety of reasons
units.function: open a feature list from an intuition, then name the reasons
units.reusable_pattern: Start from intuitively seems, then list the reasons.
information_order: intuitively seems to be difficult for a variety of reasons
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the features as measured facts yet.

units.source_excerpt: our first task was to list and quantify such characteristics, so that we could instead simply consider the vector
units.function: replace the word by the vector of its traits
units.reusable_pattern: Say the first task was to list and quantify, so that we could instead.
information_order: so that we could instead simply consider the vector
prohibited_generalizations: Do not model the word as a string.

units.source_excerpt: leading to a reasonable assumption that words with more vowels will on average be easier
units.function: label the vowel effect as an assumption, not a result
units.reusable_pattern: Use leading to a reasonable assumption.
information_order: leading to a reasonable assumption
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the vowel effect as fitted.

units.source_excerpt: excluding y, as this is a traditionally uncommon letter and hence does not align with the reasoning
units.function: exclude a letter and give the reason in the same clause
units.reusable_pattern: Exclude, then as, then hence.
information_order: excluding, as, and hence does not align
reusable_elements: does not align with the reasoning
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop y silently.

units.source_excerpt: It makes sense that words which are used more commonly will be more familiar, and hence easier
units.function: justify a predictor by familiarity
units.reusable_pattern: Use it makes sense that, and hence.
information_order: it makes sense that, and hence easier
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite a fitted coefficient here.

units.source_excerpt: Once this occurs, players get very direct hints that they can immediately put into action
units.function: say why a tile count should matter
units.reusable_pattern: Use once this occurs, then immediately.
information_order: once this occurs, immediately put into action
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define the average without the reason.

units.source_excerpt: Thus, while it may be easier to initially obtain green tiles, players may also be less likely to guess those same letters again
units.function: hold both effects of a repeated letter
units.reusable_pattern: Use while it may, may also.
information_order: while it may be easier, may also be less likely
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat repeated letters as purely helpful.

units.source_excerpt: As a result, it seems justified to consider the number of unique letters
units.function: promote a hunch to a feature with a soft verb
units.reusable_pattern: Use as a result, it seems justified to consider.
information_order: it seems justified to consider
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the feature is required.

units.source_excerpt: a reasonable question to ask is how much information
units.function: turn a definition into a question the formula will answer
units.reusable_pattern: Ask how much before writing the formula.
information_order: a reasonable question to ask is how much
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open the section with the formula.

units.source_excerpt: Conversely, target words are more difficult to guess which result in a lower amount of information
units.function: flip the guess ranking into a target ranking
units.reusable_pattern: Use conversely.
information_order: conversely, more difficult which result in lower
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the same ranking for guesses and targets.

units.source_excerpt: words which have more unusual letter placements, and hence can reasonably be assumed to be more difficult, will have a higher value
units.function: read the entropy in the same sentence that defines it
units.reusable_pattern: Give the reading with and hence can reasonably be assumed.
information_order: and hence can reasonably be assumed
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the sign of the measure unstated.

units.source_excerpt: This metric is motivated by the idea that
units.function: announce the motivation before the definition
units.reusable_pattern: Start with this metric is motivated by the idea that.
information_order: is motivated by the idea that
prohibited_generalizations: Do not start from the formula.

units.source_excerpt: if g1 is a better guess than g2 given the target word is t, we have that
units.function: state the comparison the factor must obey
units.reusable_pattern: Give the inequality as a requirement on the factor.
information_order: if better, we have that the factor is larger
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define the factor without the comparison.

units.source_excerpt: The motivation for choosing this value as opposed to the factor directly is that
units.function: justify the logarithm against the raw factor
units.reusable_pattern: Say as opposed to, then the reason.
information_order: as opposed to, the motivation is that
prohibited_generalizations: Do not take the log without saying why.

units.source_excerpt: as the average of the log exactly corresponds to the log of the geometric mean, we can effectively instead consider the expectation
units.function: swap a geometric mean for an expectation of logs
units.reusable_pattern: Name the identity, then we can effectively instead.
information_order: exactly corresponds to, we can effectively instead
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the expectation an arithmetic mean of the factors.

units.source_excerpt: We decided this was reasonable, as many common words guessed appeared to be on the list
units.function: defend a uniform distribution over thirty words by inspection
units.reusable_pattern: Use we decided this was reasonable, as.
information_order: we decided this was reasonable, as
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the distribution was estimated.

units.source_excerpt: ideally the 7-vector should be encapsulated with fewer numbers
units.function: state the compression as a wish before the distribution
units.reusable_pattern: Use ideally, should be encapsulated.
information_order: ideally should be encapsulated with fewer numbers
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the seven counts without the reason.

units.source_excerpt: it turns out that the Beta distribution has a cumulative distribution function that can fit the embedded cumulative mass function closely
units.function: report the fit as something that turned out
units.reusable_pattern: Use it turns out that, closely.
information_order: it turns out that, closely
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim an exact fit.

units.source_excerpt: As alpha increases while all else is held equal, the word is considered more difficult
units.function: read one parameter with the others held fixed
units.reusable_pattern: Use while all else is held equal.
information_order: while all else is held equal
reusable_elements: while all else is held equal
prohibited_generalizations: Do not read alpha without holding beta.

units.source_excerpt: Because of these properties, particularly the final one, alpha and beta together are an effective and simple representation
units.function: choose the representation for one property among several
units.reusable_pattern: Use because of these properties, particularly.
information_order: because of these properties, particularly the final one
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say both parameters are equally the point.

units.source_excerpt: we must use select a subset of them, as the time taken by MCMC increases significantly
units.function: cut predictors because the sampler slows, and keep the slip
units.reusable_pattern: Keep we must use select. Give the runtime as the reason.
information_order: we must use select, as the time taken increases
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repair the verb, and do not cut predictors for fit alone.

units.source_excerpt: which in turn forces less important variables to have coefficients of zero
units.function: say what the penalty does, not only what it is
units.reusable_pattern: Use which in turn forces.
information_order: which in turn forces coefficients of zero
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe the penalty as shrinkage only.

units.source_excerpt: after experimentation we set lambda to 0.1 to obtain the desired number of parameters (four)
units.function: set a tuning constant to hit a chosen count
units.reusable_pattern: Say after experimentation, to obtain the desired number.
information_order: after experimentation, to obtain the desired number
prohibited_generalizations: Do not pretend the constant was cross-validated.

units.source_excerpt: Four parameters appeared repeatedly with nonzero coefficients
units.function: keep a predictor because it survived several regressions
units.reusable_pattern: Use appeared repeatedly.
information_order: appeared repeatedly with nonzero coefficients
prohibited_generalizations: Do not keep a predictor that was nonzero once.

units.source_excerpt: We use a Bayesian model comprising three conditionally independent submodels
units.function: name the three jobs in one sentence
units.reusable_pattern: Use comprising, then name each model in parentheses.
information_order: comprising three conditionally independent submodels
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce the submodels one section later without the sentence.

units.source_excerpt: Since the effect of difficulty is not necessarily the same, we do a separate regression within each
units.function: justify three copies of the same regression
units.reusable_pattern: Use since, not necessarily the same, we do a separate.
information_order: not necessarily the same, we do a separate regression
prohibited_generalizations: Do not share one difficulty coefficient across outcomes.

units.source_excerpt: which is wide enough to be uninformative
units.function: defend a prior by its width
units.reusable_pattern: Give the prior, then which is wide enough to be uninformative.
information_order: wide enough to be uninformative
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a Normal(0, 20) prior informative.

units.source_excerpt: The model for the distribution of tries is fundamentally a Dirichlet-Multinomial model
units.function: name the family before the sampling statement
units.reusable_pattern: Use is fundamentally.
information_order: is fundamentally a
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open with the sampling equation.

units.source_excerpt: However, since there is additional variation beyond just Poisson error, we must use an overdispersed version
units.function: reject a distribution for variation it cannot hold
units.reusable_pattern: Use however, since, beyond just, we must.
information_order: beyond just, we must use an overdispersed version
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the Poisson and add a disclaimer.

units.source_excerpt: Because of the correspondence of the long-term trend with the shape of a Gamma distribution, we parameterize
units.function: borrow a shape without claiming the trend is that distribution
units.reusable_pattern: Use because of the correspondence, we parameterize.
information_order: because of the correspondence with the shape
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the reports follow a Gamma distribution.

units.source_excerpt: the probability itself is modeled as coming from a Beta distribution
units.function: put the extra variation on the probability, not on the count
units.reusable_pattern: Say the probability itself.
information_order: the probability itself is modeled as coming from
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add noise to the binomial count directly.

units.source_excerpt: which has a long tail and acts as an uninformative prior
units.function: defend a prior by its tail, and keep the doubled verb
units.reusable_pattern: Keep which is has. Say long tail, acts as uninformative.
information_order: has a long tail and acts as an uninformative prior
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repair which is has.

units.source_excerpt: Rather than computing simple point estimates, we obtain full posterior distributions
units.function: refuse the point estimate at the moment of fitting
units.reusable_pattern: Use rather than, we obtain.
information_order: rather than simple point estimates, full posterior distributions
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report a posterior mean as the fit.

units.source_excerpt: Because the three submodels are conditionally independent given the data, we run MCMC separately
units.function: turn the independence into three separate runs
units.reusable_pattern: Use because, we run separately.
information_order: conditionally independent, we run separately
reusable_elements: we run MCMC on the three submodels separately
prohibited_generalizations: Do not sample the joint model as one chain.

units.source_excerpt: The word cause is used intentionally here
units.function: flag a strong verb and then earn it
units.reusable_pattern: Say the word is used intentionally, then give the assumption that earns it.
information_order: is used intentionally here
prohibited_generalizations: Do not write cause and move on.

units.source_excerpt: if words are chosen randomly, any correlation must be due to an effect, and not due to a reverse effect or a confounding variable
units.function: close the other two explanations under the assumption
units.reusable_pattern: Name both rejected explanations: reverse effect, confounding variable.
information_order: not due to a reverse effect or a confounding variable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim causation from the coefficient alone.

units.source_excerpt: The posterior distributions of almost all of the coefficients include zero, suggesting that there is no additional effect
units.function: read an interval that contains zero as no additional effect
units.reusable_pattern: Use include zero, suggesting that.
information_order: include zero, suggesting that
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report a coefficient whose interval contains zero as an effect.

units.source_excerpt: On the contrary, the posterior for c1 is largely negative, which counteracts the effect
units.function: rescue one coefficient that goes the other way
units.reusable_pattern: Use on the contrary, which counteracts.
information_order: on the contrary, which counteracts
prohibited_generalizations: Do not fold the exception into the general claim.

units.source_excerpt: One possible causal interpretation is that the set of players who play on hard mode is more consistent
units.function: offer a mechanism as one possible reading
units.reusable_pattern: Use one possible causal interpretation is that.
information_order: one possible causal interpretation is that
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the mechanism as identified.

units.source_excerpt: Surprisingly, the coefficients are centered around zero, indicating no evidence for a periodic effect
units.function: mark a null result as a surprise
units.reusable_pattern: Open with surprisingly.
information_order: surprisingly, centered around zero, indicating no evidence
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit a null result.

units.source_excerpt: This suggests that there are insufficient data to, in combination with the other effects, reliably estimate a periodic effect
units.function: blame a null result on the data, not on the absence of the effect
units.reusable_pattern: Say insufficient data to, in combination with, reliably estimate.
information_order: insufficient data to reliably estimate
prohibited_generalizations: Do not conclude the periodic effect is zero.

units.source_excerpt: The model can be used to make predictions for past data
units.function: define retrodiction as prediction on the past
units.reusable_pattern: Say predictions for past data before showing the figure.
information_order: predictions for past data
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call a fit to the training days a forecast.

units.source_excerpt: The model seems to capture the variation in the data as well as the long-term trend
units.function: hedge the visual check
units.reusable_pattern: Use seems to capture, as well as.
information_order: seems to capture the variation as well as the trend
prohibited_generalizations: Do not say the model fits.

units.source_excerpt: shows good agreement with the truth
units.function: check one past word against its observed bars
units.reusable_pattern: Name the word, then good agreement with the truth.
information_order: good agreement with the truth
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim agreement from the aggregate plot alone.

units.source_excerpt: This can be done either for a future date and word, or for a date alone
units.function: separate a word-specific forecast from an average over words
units.reusable_pattern: Use either, or.
information_order: either for a date and word, or for a date alone
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report one without saying which.

units.source_excerpt: Notably, the posterior samples lie along the alpha equals beta line, indicating a fairly stable difficulty but less certainty about the shape
units.function: split what is stable from what is not, and keep the spelling
units.reusable_pattern: Keep certainity as printed in the source. Say stable, but less certain about the shape.
information_order: lie along the line, indicating stable but less certain
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the ratio without the uncertainty of the shape.

units.source_excerpt: This places eerie in roughly the 50th percentile of words
units.function: translate a ratio into a rank among past words
units.reusable_pattern: Use places, in roughly.
information_order: places in roughly the 50th percentile
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report 0.52 without the rank.

units.source_excerpt: The Subset Entropy predictor does not capture how difficult a word is to guess after the first guess
units.function: bound a feature by the guess it ignores
units.reusable_pattern: Say does not capture, then for instance.
information_order: does not capture how difficult after the first guess
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present subset entropy as full difficulty.

units.source_excerpt: Subset Entropy requires us to make assumptions on the distribution of first guesses
units.function: name the assumption the feature cannot avoid
units.reusable_pattern: Use requires us to make assumptions.
information_order: requires us to make assumptions
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide the guess distribution.

units.source_excerpt: Compared to traditional statistical methods, Bayesian models sampled using MCMC are extremely slow
units.function: price the posterior against a point estimate
units.reusable_pattern: Open with compared to.
information_order: compared to traditional methods, extremely slow
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the cost of the sampler.

units.source_excerpt: The model does not take into account changes in mean player skill across different days
units.function: name a time effect that was left out
units.reusable_pattern: Say does not take into account, then the thing omitted.
information_order: does not take into account
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the difficulty is skill-free.

units.source_excerpt: instead assume a stable long-term trend which may underestimate the uncertainty inherent in long-term predictions
units.function: say what the missing autocorrelation does to the intervals
units.reusable_pattern: Use instead assume, which may underestimate.
information_order: which may underestimate the uncertainty
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the long-horizon interval as calibrated.

units.source_excerpt: rather than a simple best-fit and prediction intervals that require approximations
units.function: prefer the full distribution to an interval that needs extra assumptions
units.reusable_pattern: Use rather than, that require.
information_order: rather than intervals that require approximations
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the interval is assumption-free.

units.source_excerpt: other models may not capture the asymmetry in the posterior-predicted distributions
units.function: point at a shape a symmetric interval would miss
units.reusable_pattern: Name the two skewed quantities.
information_order: may not capture the asymmetry
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim every posterior is skewed.

units.source_excerpt: The uncertainty includes not only that from true noise, but also uncertainty in the estimates of the coefficients
units.function: split noise uncertainty from parameter uncertainty
units.reusable_pattern: Use not only, but also.
information_order: not only noise, but also uncertainty in the estimates
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report a residual interval as the full uncertainty.

units.source_excerpt: which is appropriate as different aspects of word difficulty may affect these outcomes
units.function: justify separate effects by the outcomes they touch
units.reusable_pattern: Use which is appropriate as.
information_order: which is appropriate as
prohibited_generalizations: Do not share one difficulty effect without this sentence.

units.source_excerpt: cannot be exactly measured
units.function: say why two parameters are enough
units.reusable_pattern: End on cannot be exactly measured.
information_order: cannot be exactly measured
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim the two parameters are the difficulty.

units.source_excerpt: Rather than having a single, prescriptive metric, we come up with several
units.function: refuse one difficulty number at the close
units.reusable_pattern: Use rather than a single prescriptive metric.
information_order: rather than a single, prescriptive metric
prohibited_generalizations: Do not close on one score.

units.source_excerpt: The innovative aspect of the model is that it is made up of three submodels which, when conditioned upon the data, are independent
units.function: restate the one property that makes the large model tractable
units.reusable_pattern: Call it the innovative aspect, then the independence.
information_order: the innovative aspect is that
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call the model innovative for being Bayesian.

units.source_excerpt: We provide several retrodictions to confirm that our model aligns with past data
units.function: close the prediction claim with the past check
units.reusable_pattern: Use to confirm that, aligns with.
information_order: to confirm that our model aligns with past data
prohibited_generalizations: Do not close on the forecast alone.

units.source_excerpt: The references run from the No-U-Turn sampler to SciPy, seven entries
units.function: record a short reference list tied to the tools actually used
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the list short and name the tool each entry supports.
information_order: seven entries, each a tool
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent an eighth reference.

units.source_excerpt: One entry is the Oxford English Dictionary home page, used for the count of five-letter words
units.function: tie the dictionary citation to the one number it supports
units.reusable_pattern: Say what the page was used for.
information_order: used for the count
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite the dictionary for the model.

units.source_excerpt: Dear Puzzle Editor of the New York Times
units.function: address the person who chooses the word, not a general reader
units.reusable_pattern: Name the office in the greeting.
information_order: dear puzzle editor
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open the letter with the model.

units.source_excerpt: Part of what we aimed to do was discover what causes this variation
units.function: restate the aim as a cause, in the editor's terms
units.reusable_pattern: Use part of what we aimed to do.
information_order: part of what we aimed to do was
prohibited_generalizations: Do not restate the three submodels first.

units.source_excerpt: We discovered that the greatest variation in player reporting was due to the difficulty of the word
units.function: lead the letter with the finding, not the method
units.reusable_pattern: Use we discovered that, the greatest variation was due to.
information_order: we discovered that the greatest variation was due to
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open the finding with a coefficient.

units.source_excerpt: likely due to Wordle aging as a game
units.function: offer the downward trend a cause, hedged
units.reusable_pattern: Use likely due to.
information_order: likely due to
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert the cause of the decline.

units.source_excerpt: On the other hand, there was also no real effect of word difficulty on the number of players reporting playing in hard mode
units.function: pair the positive finding with the null one
units.reusable_pattern: Use on the other hand, no real effect.
information_order: on the other hand, no real effect
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report only the reports effect.

units.source_excerpt: this is indicative of more casual players leaving the game
